note_en: 起来 after a verb of perception (闻 smell, 尝 taste, 看 look, 听 listen) means "to smell / taste / look …": 闻起来很香，尝起来又麻又辣 "it smells fragrant and tastes numbing and spicy." It reports an impression rather than a fact, which is why it suits judgments like 那盘尝起来还算可以 "that plate tasted passable" — fine on its own, pale next to the cook's. English uses linking verbs ("smells," "tastes," "looks") for the same job.
